subsystems.name: Tumour antigen discovery
subsystems.role: finds the mutated proteins unique to a patient's cancer that the immune system can target.

subsystems.name: mRNA design and synthesis
subsystems.role: builds the genetic instructions for those target proteins.

subsystems.name: Lipid nanoparticle delivery
subsystems.role: wraps the mRNA so it survives in the body and enters cells.

subsystems.name: Personalised manufacturing
subsystems.role: produces a single patient's vaccine quickly and safely.

subsystems.name: Administration and immune monitoring
subsystems.role: delivers the vaccine and checks that it triggered the intended T-cell attack.

buildSteps.title: Take a tumour sample
buildSteps.detail: A biopsy or surgical specimen is preserved so its DNA and RNA can be read.

buildSteps.title: Sequence the tumour and normal tissue
buildSteps.detail: Comparing the two reveals mutations that exist only in the cancer.

buildSteps.title: Predict neoantigens
buildSteps.detail: Software ranks mutated peptide fragments by how well they bind the patient's immune type and how likely they are to provoke a T-cell response.

buildSteps.title: Design the mRNA
buildSteps.detail: Selected neoantigen sequences are encoded into one or more mRNA molecules, often with signals that boost immune recognition.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the mRNA
buildSteps.detail: Enzymes copy a DNA template into mRNA, then a cap and tail are added and the product is purified.

buildSteps.title: Formulate lipid nanoparticles
buildSteps.detail: The mRNA is mixed with lipids in a microfluidic device to form tiny particles that protect it and help it enter cells.

buildSteps.title: Test the batch
buildSteps.detail: Each personalised batch is checked for correct sequence, purity, particle size and potency before release.

buildSteps.title: Vaccinate and monitor
buildSteps.detail: The patient receives a series of injections; blood tests track T-cell responses, and imaging checks whether tumours shrink.

prerequisites.why: the COVID-19 vaccines proved mRNA can be made, formulated and given safely at large scale.
the same delivery system that carries mRNA into cells for COVID-19 vaccines works for cancer targets.
fast, affordable sequencing is needed to find each patient's unique mutations.
algorithms are improving but still cannot reliably pick the few mutations that will trigger a strong immune attack.
making a single patient's vaccine in days rather than weeks is not yet routine and remains a bottleneck.

pathway.milestone: clinical trials of personalised mRNA vaccines, often combined with checkpoint inhibitors, in melanoma, pancreatic and other cancers
pathway.unlocks: proof that the approach can shrink tumours in some patients.

pathway.milestone: faster neoantigen prediction and manufacturing that delivers a vaccine within days
pathway.unlocks: treatment for patients whose cancer is progressing quickly.

pathway.milestone: off-the-shelf vaccines targeting shared neoantigens found in many patients
pathway.unlocks: cheaper, faster treatment without waiting for a personalised batch.

pathway.milestone: use in earlier-stage disease or in people at high risk
pathway.unlocks: cancer prevention or interception before tumours spread.
